He played [[college basketball]] for [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] and was selected 14th overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. After playing two seasons for the Thunder, he was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2017, where he played for three seasons before being waived in 2019. After being waived, Payne played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on 10-day contracts before heading overseas to play with the [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). Payne returned to the NBA and signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2020, where he revitalized his career by becoming a key player off the bench, helping the team reach the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]. Since then, he has played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and the [[New York Knicks]]. ==High school career== Payne attended [[Lausanne Collegiate School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]]. He grew from {{Height|ft=5|in=5}} as a freshman to {{Height|ft=6|in=0}} as a senior. Despite leading Lausanne Collegiate to a 2013 Division II state title in Tennessee, Payne was not a heavily scouted player by collegiate programs. He was considered to be a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and was not ranked in the top 100 prospects. He was recruited by [[William Small (basketball)|William Small]] to play [[college basketball]] at [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]], choosing the Racers over a few other schools. Payne then went from a relatively unknown college recruit to a potential NBA lottery pick. ==College career== As a freshman, Payne averaged 16.8 points, 5.4 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game.{{Cite web |last=Grant |first=Michael |date=November 7, 2014 |title=Payne hopes to copy Canaan's success at Murray |url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentuckiana/2014/11/07/murray-state-basketballs-cameron-payne-hopes-copy-isaiah-canaans-success/18654085/ |access-date=November 7, 2014 |website=Courier-Journal.com |archive-date=September 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230911235644/https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentuckiana/2014/11/07/murray-state-basketballs-cameron-payne-hopes-copy-isaiah-canaans-success/18654085/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite news |last=Dauster |first=Rob |date=October 24, 2014 |title=Cameron Payne didn't expect to fill Isaiah Canaan's void at Murray State, but he did |work=[[NBC Sports]] |url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/23/cameron-payne-didnt-expect-to-fill-isaiah-canaans-void-at-murray-state-but-he-did/ |access-date=September 25, 2015 |archive-date=September 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150902021753/http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/23/cameron-payne-didnt-expect-to-fill-isaiah-canaans-void-at-murray-state-but-he-did/ |url-status=live }} He was forced to start at point guard as a freshman due to an injury to Zay Jackson and began his collegiate career registering 21 points, five boards and four assists in the team's opener at [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]]. Payne earned first-team All-OVC honors and was named Freshman of the Year by the conference.{{Cite news |last=Spears |first=Marc |date=June 21, 2015 |title=How Cameron Payne went from little-known college recruit to potential NBA lottery pick |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/how-cameron-payne-went-from-little-known-college-recruit-to-potential-nba-lottery-pick-221737745.html |access-date=September 25, 2015 |archive-date=September 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926142729/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/how-cameron-payne-went-from-little-known-college-recruit-to-potential-nba-lottery-pick-221737745.html |url-status=live }} As a sophomore, he was the [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ohio Valley Conference Player of the Year]] after he averaged 20.2 points, 6.0 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game.{{Cite web |last=Hurcomb |first=Michael |date=March 3, 2015 |title=Sophomore PG Cameron Payne takes home Ohio Valley POY honors |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25091553/sophomore-pg-cameron-payne-takes-home-ohio-valley-poy-honors |access-date=March 3, 2015 |website=CBSSports.com |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402160117/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25091553/sophomore-pg-cameron-payne-takes-home-ohio-valley-poy-honors |url-status=live }} Payne opted to declare for the NBA Draft after his sophomore season. ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2015–2017)=== During workouts before the NBA draft, Payne broke the ring finger on his non-shooting hand. The injury did not require surgery.
